about: Escape Animals sends you out from a base to find blocky animals. The open area contains hazards such as bursts of lava and terrain traps. Look for a return route before moving toward an animal, especially when the nearest path narrows.
Collecting an animal is the first half of a trip. Bring it back to the base to secure the reward. A close animal can be a good early choice when you can reach it and return through open ground.

Animals have different rarities and variants, and base upgrades affect the income they produce. Use earnings from successful short trips to improve your collection before attempting a route with more difficult obstacles.
steps: Move and check the camera
Use WASD or the arrow keys to move. Use the right mouse button to adjust the view and check the route back.
Collect an animal with E
Get close and press E. Turn toward the base once you have the animal and watch for changes along the return path.
Clear or avoid an obstacle
Use the left mouse button for the game's attack or obstacle action. Look for an open route when stopping would put the pickup at risk.
Upgrade at the base
Use F at the base to upgrade animals. Compare the cost and income from your current collection before choosing the next trip.
faq: When is an animal secured?
Return safely to the base after collecting it. The completed trip is what lets the animal contribute to your income.
Which key picks up an animal?
Press E when you are close enough to the animal.
How do I improve income at the base?
Bring back animals and use F to upgrade them at the base. Rarity and upgrades affect the value of your collection.

en.summary: Choose a class and clear dungeon waves in Stick Hero RPG. Use movement, skills and earned gold to build a character for harder encounters.
en.aboutTitle: Build around the class you want to play
about: Your first choices in Stick Hero RPG are a species and a class. Humans, elves and orcs offer different starting styles. The Gunner, Wizard, Archer and Thief classes give you different ways to attack and spend skill points.

Dungeon stages play out from the side. You move, jump and use attacks while keeping track of health and mana. Early waves are a chance to learn your class's reach and ability timing before a boss arrives.

Gold earned from battles pays for equipment and upgrades. If you are consistently running out of health before a wave ends, improve survival first. Once you can finish a wave reliably, invest in the damage or abilities you use most.
steps: Pick a species and class
Choose from the starting options. Learn one class's basic movement and attacks before comparing another.
Move and jump through the stage
Use A and D or the left and right arrows to move. Press Space, W or the up arrow to jump.
Aim attacks and use skills
Hold the left mouse button and move the pointer to aim your in-game attack. Use the number keys for equipped skills.
Set a priority for earned gold
When a stage ends, compare upgrades against the part of the encounter that gave you trouble. Spend toward one goal and try another wave.
faq: Which keys trigger skills?
Use the number keys assigned to your skills. Check your current abilities before entering the next wave.
Can I restart the current round?
The published controls assign E to reset the round.
How should I spend early skill points?
Start with abilities that support the class you actually use in fights. Monitor health and mana before deciding whether to invest in survival or damage.

en.summary: Slide and merge evolving creature tiles in 2048 Rogue. Leave room for new tiles and choose between a story route and endless play.
en.aboutTitle: Leave a route for the next matching tile
about: Each arrow input moves the board in one direction. Identical icons combine into a higher form, and a new tile can appear after a move. Look at the whole board before sliding, since a useful merge can also shift pieces you were saving.

A corner gives you a place to build a high-tier creature while lower forms line up beside it. Read the rows that feed that corner. If a slide separates two matching icons, check whether another direction keeps them together.

Story mode adds structured objectives and narrative fragments. Endless mode lets you focus on keeping the board playable. Undo can help you review a move that closed an important gap. Check how the board changes before repeating the slide.
steps: Slide with the arrow keys
Choose a direction and watch all tiles move together. Matching icons can merge into a higher form.
Keep a space beside a developed tile
Try building toward one edge so you can feed that tile from a neighboring row. Check which other lines will shift first.
Check what a move does to the board
Before sliding into a near-full side, look for at least one merge or opening to use on the following move.
Review a close call with Undo
Use Undo when available to revisit a slide that separated a pair or trapped several tiles. Compare another direction before committing.
faq: What ends a run?
The run ends when you have no legal moves left.
What do matching tiles turn into?
Two identical icons merge into a higher form. The game uses evolving creatures and objects as its tiles.
How do Story and Endless differ?
Story adds objectives and narrative fragments as you advance. Endless emphasizes keeping the board open and merging for longer.

en.summary: Switch lanes with one click in Tap Road. Dodge numbered blocks as the neon road speeds up and collect spheres to unlock tracks and ball designs.
en.aboutTitle: Watch the next pair of blocks instead of the ball
about: The ball rolls forward automatically along two lanes. Click to move it to the opposite lane before it reaches a numbered block. You score by dodging obstacles, and the road gets faster during the run.

Look beyond the nearest block to see which lane the one after it occupies. Changing lanes too early can put you in the path of a closer obstacle. Changing back immediately can leave you with too little time for the next move.

Spheres can buy tracks and ball designs, while challenges offer additional rewards. Take a sphere when the approach and exit are clear. A clean run gives you more chances to see how the obstacle pattern changes at higher speeds.
steps: Click to switch lanes
One mouse click sends the ball into the other lane. Wait until the next action actually needs a lane change.
Look two blocks ahead
Identify which lane holds the nearer block. Then check whether you will need to switch back for the following one.
Take spheres on a clear route
Collect spheres when they are along the lane you can hold safely. Skip ones that would put you in the path of a numbered block.
Use challenges to pick a goal
Check the listed challenges between runs. Focus on a single goal while you practice changes at higher speeds.
faq: Can I slow down the ball?
The ball moves forward and speeds up automatically. Your control switches it between the two lanes.
How is the score counted?
Your score reflects how many obstacles you dodge. Spheres are a separate pickup.
What can I buy with spheres?
Use collected spheres toward more tracks and ball designs.

en.summary: Build power, rotate and land on your feet in Flip Rush. Practice the release timing across parkour courses with different takeoff points.
en.aboutTitle: Release the rotation with the landing zone in view
about: Flip Rush asks you to land on your feet inside a marked area. Hold the left mouse button or Space to build power and rotate. Release as you approach the position you need for the landing.
The opening tutorial walks you through the motion. Use it to see how long a short rotation takes. On later layouts, check the height and position of the next target before deciding how long to hold.

Finishing a location's levels opens the next setting. A takeoff that works in the gym may leave you rotating too late on a mountain or city stage. Start with a clean landing before trying to earn more points from another rotation.
steps: Learn the hold and release in the tutorial
Hold left-click or Space to build the movement, then release to prepare for landing.
Read where the target begins
Check whether the landing zone is close below you or farther away. Use that distance to judge when you should stop rotating.
Correct one part after a missed attempt
If you reach the area while still turning, try releasing sooner. If you fall short of the area, compare the next takeoff without changing everything at once.
Complete a location to advance
Finish the stages in the current setting to open the next. Learn the first landing there before attempting longer combinations.
faq: Can I use Space instead of the mouse?
Yes. Holding Space or the left mouse button builds power and rotation. Release to set up your landing.
What counts as a clean landing?
Finish on your feet inside the marked target zone. An awkward landing can lower the score or fail the attempt.
How do I open another location?
Complete the stages in the current location. The next setting then becomes available.

en.summary: Ride a sled through changing winter courses in Slope Rider 3D. Jump past logs and gaps, collect gift boxes and try Normal or Hard mode.
en.aboutTitle: Set up the next turn before you leave the snow
about: Slope Rider 3D sends you down a changing winter course. Rolling logs, falling trees and snow boulders can block space you planned to use. Read where the obstacle will be when you arrive, especially if you need to jump.

Normal and Hard modes let you choose the challenge. Use Normal to learn how long your sled stays in the air and how quickly it can steer after landing. Try Hard once you can set up the turn after a jump without swinging across the whole track.

Gift boxes unlock sleds with different performance traits. A quicker sled can give you less time between nearby obstacles. Try a new sled over a few clear descents to get used to its steering and jump timing.
steps: Steer left or right
Use the arrow keys to guide the sled. Make a clear move before the path narrows.
Jump with the up arrow or Space
Use either key to clear a log or gap. Look for a clear landing strip before leaving the snow.
Pick up gifts when you can exit safely
Follow a gift line when there is room after it for your next turn. Leave a box behind if it is beside a moving hazard.
Compare Normal and Hard
Practice judging the distance to a log on Normal. Use the same look-ahead habit when you try Hard.
faq: Is the course identical on every descent?
No. The game changes the terrain and obstacle placement, so watch the current slope instead of memorizing a single route.
What can I use gift boxes for?
Collected gifts can unlock additional sleds with different handling, jumping or speed traits.
How can I jump and steer with separate controls?
Use the left and right arrows to steer and Space to jump. The up arrow also jumps.

en.summary: Collect Brainrots and get back to base before waves sweep the course. Use trenches for shelter and upgrade your speed, carrying capacity and base.
en.aboutTitle: Pick a return route with a trench in reach
about: Brainrots appear on platforms along the course. Collect one and bring it back to base to start earning income from it. A farther platform can offer a more valuable pickup, but it also leaves a longer trip back.

A tsunami can sweep the course while you are out collecting. Trenches give you a place to wait for it to pass. Before heading farther out, look for a trench you can reach from the platform you are aiming for.
Income from returned units pays for improvements. Speed helps when the trip itself takes too long. Capacity lets you carry more in one outing, while extra slots give you room for more units at base.
steps: Set out and check the route
Move with WASD or the arrow keys. Use the right mouse button to adjust the camera so you can see the platforms and nearby trenches.
Pick up a Brainrot
Press E when you are close enough to a unit. Use Space to jump over gaps in the course and check your landing before leaving the platform.
Get out of the wave's path
If a wave approaches and the base is too far away, aim for a trench and wait for the wave to pass before continuing.
Use the income to improve the next trip
Return the Brainrot to base. Consider a speed upgrade if travel time keeps cutting your trips short, or capacity if you often leave reachable units behind.
faq: Where can I wait for a wave to pass?
The trenches along the running track serve as safe zones. Look for one before you head into a distant section.
When do Brainrots start earning income?
Bring them back and place them at your base. Units still on the course do not contribute to the base.
What can I upgrade between trips?
The game lets you improve movement speed, carrying capacity and the number of available base slots.

en.summary: Time a cannon launch in Ragdoll Launcher. Guide the ragdoll through the air, use boosts and earn upgrades for longer runs.
en.aboutTitle: Judge the launch and first bounce separately
about: A moving cannon and a power indicator determine the start of the run. Watch the aim and release timing before clicking. A strong launch still needs an angle that carries the character into an open part of the course.

You can drag the mouse to make small adjustments once the ragdoll is airborne. A trampoline or another in-game boost can keep the flight going. Scan for a clean way through before making a large adjustment toward one.

Distance earns rewards that help unlock improvements. Watch the first landing on early attempts. If you lose momentum immediately, compare a different launch timing before changing the upgrade you are saving for.
steps: Watch the indicator before clicking
Wait until the cannon points toward a clear route and the power indicator is near the part of its range you want.
Make a small correction in the air
Drag the mouse to guide the ragdoll. Let the movement settle before making another change.
Look for a reachable boost
Use a trampoline or other boost when it is near the flight path. Keep a clear route through the next set of obstacles.
Compare two launches
Try similar power with a slightly different aim. See which one reaches a better first bounce before investing in another upgrade.
faq: Which control launches the ragdoll?
Click when the cannon and power indicator are where you want them.
Can I adjust direction after launch?
Yes. Drag the mouse in the air to guide the character toward a landing or boost.
Why do runs with similar power end at different distances?
Launch angle, bounces and obstacles change the path after takeoff. Watch where the first landing occurs in each run.

en.summary: Face zombie waves in Dead Strike. Learn the controls, use breaks to reload and spend mission rewards on upgrades for later encounters.
en.aboutTitle: Learn how each upgrade changes a wave
about: Dead Strike puts you in ruined urban game maps with waves of zombies. Some enemies reach you more quickly than others. Follow the movement on screen before committing to one target.

Your in-game loadout can change during a mission. Keep track of the current magazine and use a break between waves to reload. Check the selected weapon after switching so the next shot behaves the way you expect.

Mission rewards can buy upgrades to attributes such as reload speed and magazine capacity. Pay attention to where a run gets difficult. If frequent reloads interrupt a wave, compare improvements that address that part of the game.
steps: Move with the keyboard
Use WASD or the arrow keys to reposition your character and keep the approaching wave in view.
Aim and fire with the mouse
Move the pointer to aim at an on-screen zombie, then click to fire the active game weapon.
Reload and switch between waves
Press R to reload and use the mouse wheel to switch the active weapon. Check the new selection before the next group arrives.
Spend a mission reward on one improvement
Compare the listed changes to damage, reload speed or magazine size. Test the upgrade in a familiar mission before spending again.
faq: How do I change weapons?
Scroll the mouse wheel to switch the active in-game weapon.
Which key reloads?
Press R. A break between waves gives you time to complete the reload.
What can mission currency improve?
The game offers upgrades such as damage, accuracy, reload speed and magazine size, as well as equipment unlocks.

en.summary: Click the meme character for points in Goo Goo Gaga Clicker. Buy per-click or automatic upgrades and use temporary bonuses to reach new characters.
en.aboutTitle: Spend points on how you want to earn them
about: Clicking the character earns points for your first upgrades. Some purchases raise the value of each click. Others earn points automatically while the game runs, giving you a different way to reach the next milestone.
The bonus bar rewards active clicking. When it fills, the points from each click double. If a temporary power-up appears, watch its effect before using your balance on a permanent change.

New forms appear as you reach milestones. Try one upgrade and watch your next round of earnings before buying again. Compare points from a short clicking burst with what the automatic upgrades produce when you pause.
steps: Click the character to earn points
Start on the main screen and watch the total after each click. Open the upgrade options when you can afford one.
Pick an active or automatic upgrade
Choose more points per click for an active session. Pick automatic production when you want the total to keep rising between clicks.
Watch the bonus bar
Track the bar while you click. Use the doubled per-click reward while it is active.
Review the next milestone
Check the next upgrade cost after a bonus ends. Save toward a purchase that supports the way you plan to play.
faq: Do I have to click continuously?
Some upgrades produce points automatically while the game runs. Early clicks help you afford the first of those upgrades.
What happens when the bonus bar fills?
It doubles the points earned per click. Watch the bar to see when the bonus ends.
How do new characters appear?
New character forms are unlocked as you reach progression milestones.

en.summary: Flip a bottle across living-room furniture in Bottle Hop. Time single and double jumps, avoid hazards and collect rewards for bottle skins.
en.aboutTitle: Choose the next landing before the bottle takes off
about: Bottle Hop turns shelves, tables and speakers into stepping stones. Click to flip the bottle off its current surface and aim for the next one. Level runs ask you to reach the finish without touching the floor.

A double click gives you an extra jump for larger gaps. Use it when the next surface is beyond the reach of a single flip. On short hops, the extra movement can carry the bottle past an otherwise easy landing.

Later layouts add moving hazards, such as fans and falling objects. Watch the landing area long enough to see whether it stays clear. Endless mode lets you try a longer sequence of flips, and collected gems and caps can unlock more skins.
steps: Click once for a nearby surface
Look at the closest piece of furniture and tap the left mouse button to flip toward it.
Use a double jump for wider gaps
Double-click when a single flip will fall short. Check where the bottle can come down after the extra jump.
Wait for a moving hazard to clear
Watch how a fan or other moving object affects the landing area. Start the jump when there is room to reach the surface.
Practice a short route before Endless
Use level stages to get used to the distance of a single flip. In Endless, apply that timing when the route gives you a narrow platform.
faq: Which input makes the bottle flip?
Use a left click for a single flip. A double click gives you the extra jump.
What happens if the bottle touches the floor?
The level attempt ends. Look for a piece of furniture you can reach with the jump you have available.
What are gems and gold caps for?
They help unlock bottle skins you can use in later runs.

en.summary: Ride a motocross bike over narrow platforms and high ramps. Control your speed and pitch to reach the finish and earn up to three stars.
about: Build enough speed before a wide gap. Once airborne, use forward or backward lean to line up both wheels with the landing.
A checkpoint gives you another shot at a difficult stretch. Use it to compare a slower approach with a more aggressive launch.
steps: Set your speed
Ease off before a narrow landing and accelerate on the approach to wider gaps.
Level the bike
Lean to follow the angle of the landing, then resume accelerating once your wheels touch down.
faq: Why do I crash right after landing?
Check the angle of your bike and the speed you carry onto the platform. A flatter landing gives you more room to correct.

en.summary: Slide through rally checkpoints before the clock runs out and adapt your turns to gravel, asphalt and mud.
about: Survival mode keeps sending you to new checkpoints. Each one adds time, so a steady run matters more than a single long slide.
Challenge stages give you targets such as timed laps or a drift score. Use the surface to choose an entry speed for each turn.
steps: Steer into a turn
Use A and D or the arrow keys. Tap Space for a handbrake turn and straighten before the next checkpoint.
Brake before slippery sections
Use S or the down arrow to slow down. Mud gives you less room to correct after the car starts sliding.
faq: Why does the timer keep running after a checkpoint?
Each checkpoint gives you extra seconds for the next stretch. In Survival, the bonus gets smaller as you advance.

en.summary: Guide a line of wheelbarrows through fields of crops. Sell your harvest and grow the line so you can cover more ground on the next pass.
about: You start with three wheelbarrows. Steer along the outline of each crop pattern first so you can spot any rows you missed.
Longer wheelbarrow lines cover wider strips. Animal helpers can harvest alongside you as you unlock farms with different fields and crops.
steps: Move through the field
Use WASD or the arrow keys. Leave room to turn at the end of a row.
Spend your harvest
Sell crops and increase the size of your wheelbarrow line when repeated passes are slowing you down.
faq: What makes golden crops worth collecting?
Golden crops sell for more than ordinary crops. Make a short detour when one is near your route.

en.summary: Send colour-matched ants to carry away blocks and reveal a 3D pixel-art figure. Plan your moves around five waiting slots.
about: Each ant box goes into one of five slots. Its ants carry away reachable blocks of the same colour until the box is cleared.
White rings mark blocks that ants can reach. Removing those blocks can expose new ones underneath, so check the sculpture after every choice.
steps: Start with an exposed colour
Click an ant box that matches several reachable blocks. Clearing the box makes its slot available again.
Save room for the next colour
Check which blocks a move will uncover before filling the last waiting slot.
faq: What happens if I pick a blocked colour?
The box waits until matching blocks become reachable. The level can jam if all five slots are occupied by colours that cannot move.

en.summary: Compare characters to the target picture, then open surprise boxes and build a collection you can dress up.
about: Matching characters depends on small visual details. Compare faces, colours and accessories before committing to a choice.
Surprise sets add more characters to the collection. Try different clothes and accessories once you have unlocked them.
steps: Look closely at the target
Check the face and outfit first, then compare any small details that distinguish the closest candidates.
Open sets as you progress
Look through the collection after opening a box to see which characters and items are new.
faq: Is matching based only on colour?
No. Similar colours can appear on different characters, so compare the face and accessories as well.

en.summary: Rotate the neon tower so a bouncing ball drops through platform gaps. Chain several drops to trigger Fire Mode and avoid red blocks on ordinary bounces.
about: Each bounce buys a moment to line the tower up with the next opening. Watch the platform below the ball while it is in the air.
Dropping through several gaps in a row can activate Fire Mode. Use that brief window to keep descending through barriers.
steps: Rotate the tower
Drag sideways with the mouse or use the left and right arrow keys to bring a gap under the ball.
Look down the tower
Line up consecutive openings when you can. Check for red blocks before letting the ball fall.
faq: What does Fire Mode do?
A long drop can make the ball smash through platforms for a short time. When it ends, watch for red blocks again.

en.summary: Curve free kicks around a defensive wall and past the goalkeeper. Adjust direction, power and spin as the targets get harder to reach.
about: A straight shot can work with a clear path to goal. If the wall blocks your angle, add spin to bend the ball toward an open corner.
Later stadiums introduce moving defenders and wind. Watch the keeper and pick your target before starting the swipe.
steps: Choose a target
Look for a gap near a post or above the wall, then drag to send the ball toward it.
Adjust the curve
If the ball hits the wall, change your swipe angle or spin on the next attempt. Keep the amount of power similar until the curve works.
faq: Why does the same shot miss in a different stadium?
Wind and moving obstacles can change the shot. Check where the ball is pushed off course and adjust the next swipe.

en.summary: Fire coloured marbles into a moving chain. Match three or more of a colour and clear the track before the chain reaches the skull pit.
about: Close a gap between two groups of the same colour to set up a chain reaction. If the current marble has no useful shot, check the reserve colour.
Filling the progress bar stops new marbles from entering. You still need to clear the chain already on the track to finish the level.
steps: Find a matching group
Aim with the mouse and left-click to fire. A match needs three or more marbles of the same colour.
Use the reserve
Right-click to swap the current and reserve marbles when the other colour gives you a better shot.
faq: Why is the level still going after the bar fills?
The bar stops new arrivals. Remove the marbles already on the track before they reach the end.

en.summary: Stay on the rear wheel as long as you can. Feather the throttle and brake, then try tricks and stars to multiply your score.
about: Holding the gas lifts the front wheel. Too much throttle can tip the bike backward, while braking lowers the front wheel.
Tail scrapes, tricks and stars can multiply the score. Get comfortable balancing a basic wheelie before combining bonuses.
steps: Lift the front wheel
Hold D, Right Arrow or Space to accelerate. Ease off when the front wheel climbs too far.
Correct the angle
Use A or Left Arrow to brake. Once you can hold a steady angle, try W to stand on the seat or S to perform a trick.
faq: Do earned points count after a fall?
Yes, the run ends, but you keep the points and coins earned during the attempt.

en.summary: Restore a family farm, grow crops and turn your harvest into goods for shops and delivery orders.
about: Check the quest list at the car to see which repairs and crops to start with. Crops keep growing while you are away.
Feed animals to collect ingredients for workshops. Truck orders earn coins and experience, and a train station opens larger deliveries later on.
steps: Open the quest list
Interact with the car and follow the early tasks to repair buildings and plant wheat.
Choose a delivery
Check what the truck needs before selling ingredients at the roadside shop. Keep enough for recipes in progress.
faq: Will my fields grow while I am away?
Yes. Come back to harvest, then use crops in workshops or sell them through available orders.

en.summary: Build cars from the chassis up and finish each one to the customer's specifications.
about: Fit the wheels, seats and engine before working on the bodywork and paint.
New orders bring different vehicles into the garage, and finished jobs earn money for workshop upgrades.
steps: Assemble the car
Drag each part into the corresponding slot on the car.
Finish the order
Check the customer's requested finish before painting and polishing the car.
faq: What do finished jobs unlock?
New orders give you more vehicle types to build. You can also spend your earnings on tools and garage upgrades.

en.summary: Take a stunt bike over steep ramps, control its tilt in the air and land on both wheels.
about: Build speed before long jumps, then slow down on narrow platforms where there is little room for corrections.
Coins earned from missions help unlock better bikes for harder courses.
steps: Control your speed
Hold W or the up arrow to accelerate. Press S or the down arrow to brake.
Level the bike
Use A and D or the left and right arrows to tilt. Press the spacebar in the air to flip.
faq: How can I land more reliably?
Pull out of the flip early enough to line up both wheels with the landing ramp.

en.summary: Connect matching numbers in any direction and combine them into a higher-value tile.
about: You can link identical tiles horizontally, vertically and diagonally in the same chain.
Each merge changes the board. Look for a chain that also leaves useful pairs within reach for your next move.
steps: Trace a chain
Drag through neighboring tiles with the same number.
Check the new layout
After a merge, look around the new tile for another match.
faq: When does a run end?
The run ends when there are no matching tiles left that you can link.

en.summary: Cast from the shore, time your reeling and build a collection of fish from different waters.
about: Your first rod is enough to start fishing around the island. Gold from catches helps you upgrade your gear.
Boats open up waters farther from shore. Check the fish index to see which species you still need.
steps: Get to the water
Move with WASD or the arrow keys. Press 1 on the numeric keypad to equip the starter rod.
Cast and reel
Use the left mouse button for fishing actions. Follow the prompts as the fish struggles.
faq: How do I find new species?
Take a boat out to new fishing spots and check your catches against the fish index.

en.summary: Skip a stone across the water, steer around logs and buoys, and see how far it goes.
about: A well-timed release gives the stone more speed at the start.
Power gates restore speed during the run. Distance earns coins for upgrades such as launch strength and bounce.
steps: Set up your throw
Drag downward, watch the power meter and release in the marked zone.
Steer the stone
Drag left or right after launch to dodge obstacles and reach power gates.
faq: Why does the stone sink?
It sinks when it loses too much speed or hits an obstacle.

en.summary: Use two flippers to keep the ball in play and bounce it into gems.
about: Breaking gems raises your score, and more bumpers appear as you score.
The bumpers can send the ball back at a new angle. Keep your eye on its return path.
steps: Work the flippers
Use the left and right arrows or click the flippers on screen.
Aim for a gem
Wait until the ball reaches a flipper, then hit it toward an open part of the table.
faq: Why does the table get crowded?
Extra bumpers appear for every ten points, so the ball has more surfaces to bounce off.

en.summary: Keep a planet in orbit around a black hole while dodging asteroids and other planets.
about: Gravity draws your planet inward whenever you let go. Firing the thruster pushes it farther out.
Flying closer to the black hole improves your score, but gives you less room to dodge.
steps: Move outward
Hold the mouse button to fire the thruster and push away from the black hole.
Move inward
Release the button and let gravity bring the planet closer.
faq: How can I avoid an asteroid?
Watch where it crosses your orbit and change your distance from the black hole before you reach that point.

en.summary: Steer a drifting spaceship through waves of enemies, picking up ammo and power-ups as you go.
about: Your shots follow the direction your ship faces, so start your turn before the target reaches you.
Destroyed enemies can drop coins and ammo. Coins help unlock other ships.
steps: Steer and brake
Turn with A and D or the left and right arrows. Boost with W or the up arrow and brake with Shift.
Fire at enemies
Press the spacebar or click to shoot. Press B to use a bomb.
faq: How do I replenish ammunition?
Look for ammo pickups dropped by defeated enemies.

en.summary: Choose movement cards and guide a golf ball into the hole before your hand runs out.
about: Each card sets how the ball will travel. Slopes, sand and water change which route makes sense.
You have a limited set of cards per hole, so work out where each shot will leave the ball.
steps: Choose and aim
Click a card and aim the shot with the mouse.
Plan the follow-up
Before taking the shot, check that a card still in your hand can reach the hole from the landing spot.
faq: Why save a shorter card?
A short shot can help you finish when a longer one would send the ball past the hole.

en.summary: Cut through brick walls with a rotary saw and catch the falling bricks to earn coins.
about: Fuel runs down as you work. A cut underneath a section can bring several bricks down in one pass.
Spend coins on upgrades such as a longer saw or a larger fuel tank.
steps: Guide the saw
Drag the mouse to cut the wall and let the loose bricks fall into the bucket.
Watch your fuel
Pick up fuel cans and start cuts where the most bricks are likely to fall.
faq: Do I keep my coins if the fuel runs out?
Yes. Coins earned during the run can still go toward upgrades.

en.summary: Skate across rooftops, jump the gaps and collect coins along the way.
about: Your skater moves on their own. Read the next roof before jumping so you know where you can land.
Collect the letters of FANCY to fly above the rooftops for a short time.
steps: Jump at the edge
Click or press the spacebar or up arrow just before a gap.
Jump higher
Press the jump control twice when you need extra height.
faq: What ends a run?
Falling between buildings or crashing into an obstacle ends the run.

en.summary: Combine two animals into a hybrid, then explore, gather materials and build a base.
about: A hybrid can inherit different abilities and traits from its two animals.
Explore before settling down so you can choose a base location near the resources you need.
steps: Make a hybrid
Pick two animals from the list and try out the resulting creature.
Build a base
Gather materials and use them to make tools and structures.
faq: Why try another animal pair?
Different pairs can produce hybrids better suited to exploration, combat or survival.

en.summary: Deploy dinosaurs and protect their egg from waves of human attackers.
about: Each dinosaur has its own abilities. Place units where they can interrupt enemies on their way to the egg.
Coins let you strengthen dinosaurs and defenses as later waves get tougher.
steps: Set up a defense
Click to deploy a dinosaur along an approach to the egg.
Stop a crowd
Click to launch projectiles or trigger a special ability when attackers bunch together.
faq: How do I clear a level?
Keep the egg intact until the last wave is over.

en.summary: Steer a neon ball along sloping rooftops and dodge red blocks without falling off the track.
about: The ball rolls forward on its own across narrow platforms, tilted surfaces and tunnels.
Speed pads accelerate the ball automatically. Start lining up the next stretch before you reach a pad.
steps: Steer the ball
Press A or the left arrow to move left. Press D or the right arrow to move right.
Look beyond the next block
Choose a line that leaves room to approach the next platform.
faq: How is the score counted?
Your score depends on the number of track sections you complete before crashing or falling.

en.summary: Aim a puck through a maze and slide it into the hole in one shot.
about: Dragging back farther gives the puck more speed. Green pads bounce it onward, while pink walls end the attempt.
Check where moving obstacles will be when the puck reaches them.
steps: Aim and release
Drag backward from the puck to set direction and power, then let go.
Use the bounce pads
Aim for a green pad when a direct shot cannot reach the hole.
faq: Can I steer after launch?
The puck follows the path of the shot. Set the angle and power before releasing it.

en.summary: Drive around two intersecting loops and time your speed changes to avoid traffic at the crossing.
about: The car keeps moving on its own. Watch traffic on the other loop before entering the shared crossing.
Completed laps earn points and currency. More cars join the loops as you keep going.
steps: Accelerate through a gap
Press D or the up arrow when there is room to clear the crossing.
Slow down for traffic
Press A or the down arrow to let another car pass first.
faq: When should I change speed?
Make the adjustment before the crossing, while you still have room to speed up or slow down.

en.summary: Fire colored bombs into matching sections of a spinning wheel and keep your streak going.
about: The wheel changes speed, so watch how fast the target is moving before firing.
Matching shots build combos and earn coins. A shot that lands in the wrong color ends the run.
steps: Find the matching section
Check the bomb's color and follow the corresponding part of the wheel.
Fire at the right moment
Click as the matching section reaches the firing line.
faq: What do longer streaks earn?
Combos can multiply your score and help you unlock new bomb styles.

en.summary: Play one-on-one street basketball and get to seven points before your opponent.
about: Time your jumps to contest shots and save some stamina for your next drive to the basket.
Three baskets in a row activate fire mode and boost your attack.
steps: Get into position
Move with A and D or the arrow keys. Press the spacebar to jump or contest a shot.
Set shot power
Hold the spacebar or the left mouse button to adjust the power of a shot or dunk.
faq: When should I jump on defense?
Wait until the opponent commits to the shot so you are in the air when the ball goes up.

en.summary: Aim your tennis shots through glowing hoops to score points and advance through tournaments.
about: Each hoop changes the angle you need for the shot. Move into position before lining up your swing.
Tournament wins unlock tougher matches and give you more courts and players to discover.
steps: Move into position
Use WASD or the arrow keys to reach the ball.
Aim and hit
Hold A or D or the left or right arrow to aim, then release to hit the ball.
faq: How do I score?
Send the ball through the glowing hoop.

en.summary: Bounce a jelly across moving platforms, dodge hazards and collect golden drops along the way.
about: The jelly moves forward on its own. Some platforms shift before you land, so watch where they are headed.
Missing a platform or hitting an obstacle ends the run. Pick up golden drops when a safe landing is in reach.
steps: Time your jump
Click just before the jelly reaches the edge of the platform.
Pick a landing
Watch the next platform's movement and jump when there is enough room to land.
faq: Should I chase every golden drop?
Keep to the safer route if a drop would pull you away from the next platform.

en.searchTitle: Bike Hill 3D – Downhill bike racing
en.summary: Race downhill in Bike Hill 3D. Dodge trees and bumps, pick up speed boosts and pass rival cyclists before the finish line.
about: Riders start together at the top of a hill. Trees and bumps can force you to change lanes as you build speed.
Look for an open stretch after each boost. A clear route gives you more room to pass another rider.
steps: Choose a clear line
Steer around trees and bumps early so you have room to pass.
Use speed boosts
Collect a boost when you can stay on a clear route after picking it up.
faq: How do I unlock more tracks?
Complete races to open new levels.

en.searchTitle: Park Empire – Theme park management
en.summary: Build a theme park in Park Empire. Reinvest admission revenue in rides, ticket booths and parking as visitor numbers grow.
about: Start with a small park and use admission fees to open attractions such as the Ferris Wheel.
Ride upgrades can improve capacity and ticket revenue. As crowds grow, watch the entrance and parking as well as the rides.
steps: Open your first attraction
Spend early admission revenue on a ride to give visitors more to do.
Upgrade park capacity
Add ticket booths or parking when arrivals start to outgrow the entrance.
faq: Which rides can I unlock?
Later attractions include roller coasters, water rides and haunted houses.

en.searchTitle: Funny Wheels – Wheelchair obstacle course
en.summary: Control each wheel separately in Funny Wheels. Cross shifting platforms, dodge swinging traps and race to checkpoints.
about: Each wheel has its own control. Moving them together helps you roll forward, while controlling one wheel lets you turn.
The obstacle course includes slick slopes and moving platforms. Checkpoints let you practise the next stretch without starting over.
steps: Move both wheels
Use the left and right arrow keys to control the corresponding wheels.
Retry a tricky section
Press R to return to your checkpoint and try the obstacle again.
faq: Is there a race mode?
Wheel Race pits you against three rivals on themed courses.

en.searchTitle: Retro Football – Arcade American football
en.summary: Call the plays in Retro Football, a 6-on-6 American football game with passing routes, blitzes and a Retro Cup to chase.
about: Choose one of four plays before each snap. On offense, the choice determines whether you look for a running lane or an open receiver.
On defense, compare zone coverage, man-to-man assignments and blitzes. A blitz can pressure the quarterback but leaves fewer players in coverage.
steps: Pick an offensive play
Look for an open running lane or a route that gives your receiver space.
Read the defense
Throw to a receiver who has room to catch the ball and avoid forcing a deep pass into traffic.
faq: How many players are on each side?
Each team fields six players.

en.searchTitle: Slope Rider City – Endless 3D sledding
en.summary: Steer a sled through snowy city streets in Slope Rider City. Dodge traffic, jump onto vehicle roofs and find elevated routes.
about: Your sled moves forward automatically. Watch the junctions for cross traffic and look for ramps that open a route above the street.
Flashing headlights warn you that a car is about to charge. Changing lanes early leaves more room to get out of its path.
steps: Read the next junction
Look across the road before passing through an intersection.
Take the high route
Line up with a ramp early if you want to jump onto a vehicle roof.
faq: Does the route change between runs?
Yes. The game shuffles its maps between runs.

en.searchTitle: Dino Game: Tides – Underwater dinosaur runner
en.summary: Run and swim through Dino Game: Tides. Dodge coral and land obstacles, earn shells from your score and buy upgrades.
about: The T-Rex crosses rocky trails and desert stretches before heading underwater. The hazards change with the terrain.
Underwater movement slows down, and jumps carry you higher. Leave space for the longer descent when coral or anchors are ahead.
steps: Adjust your jumps
Wait for a clear landing area before jumping past an underwater obstacle.
Spend the shells you earn
Visit the shop after a run to buy equipment or permanent upgrades.
faq: How do I earn shells?
You earn one shell for each full 1,000 points scored in a run.

en.searchTitle: Dino Game: Meteor Strike – Dinosaur meteor survival
en.summary: Dodge falling meteors in Dino Game: Meteor Strike. Read the warning shadows, survive 20 waves and face two bosses.
about: A flashing mark shows where each meteor will land. The flashes speed up as impact approaches.
Later waves bring larger meteors and showers. Move into open space early so you can react when several shadows appear together.
steps: Watch the ground
Move away as soon as a warning shadow opens beneath you.
Plan an escape route
When marks overlap, look beyond the nearest shadow for a clear stretch.
faq: Can I retry a wave?
Yes. A checkpoint lets you restart the failed wave.

en.searchTitle: Bounce Blast – Arcade launcher
en.summary: Launch a wrestler into a crowd of gummies in Bounce Blast. Chain bounces, build momentum and upgrade your next run.
about: Drag and release to launch. Landing on gummies sends the wrestler bouncing again and can extend the run.
Different wrestlers have their own abilities. Try the downward slam when you can see a dense group below you.
steps: Aim the launch
Drag to set up the shot, then release to send your wrestler flying.
Keep bouncing
Look for groups of gummies where you can land and carry your momentum forward.
faq: What can I play after the story?
The game offers Stopwatch mode and an endless Rift.

en.searchTitle: Obby Bicycle – Bicycle parkour
en.summary: Ride across floating tracks in Obby Bicycle. Jump wide gaps, balance on narrow ledges and reach the next checkpoint.
about: The bike carries more speed than a character on foot, so you can jump farther. Narrow platforms leave less room to correct your landing.
If you fall, you can resume at a checkpoint. Slow down before a narrow turn, then build speed again where the track gives you room.
steps: Steer your bicycle
Use WASD or the arrow keys to move, steer and reverse.
Jump across gaps
Use Space to jump. Line the bike up with the landing before you take off.
faq: What happens if I fall off?
You return to the nearest checkpoint.

en.searchTitle: Parkour Block Maker – Block parkour and level editor
en.summary: Jump over lava in Parkour Block Maker. Reach the purple portal, then build and test your own floating obstacle course.
about: First-person parkour courses pair narrow platforms with ice blocks, jump pads and drops into lava.
The level editor lets you lay out a course and see whether its jumps work. Test the distance between blocks before adding harder obstacles.
steps: Plan your landing
Look at the next block before starting a jump, especially on ice.
Test your own route
Place several blocks in the editor and try the jumps in sequence.
faq: Where does a course end?
Look for the purple exit portal.

en.searchTitle: Moto Cabbie Simulator – Motorcycle taxi simulator
en.summary: Pick up passengers in Moto Cabbie Simulator. Accept calls, navigate traffic and earn fares to unlock more motorbikes.
about: Each job begins with a phone call. Once you accept, the pickup appears on the map and is marked on the sidewalk.
The destination appears after the passenger gets on. Brake before tight turns so you can carry the passenger through traffic safely.
steps: Pick up your passenger
Accept the call and drive into the green pickup circle.
Ride to the destination
Use WASD or the arrow keys to drive and Space to brake.
faq: How do I unlock new bikes?
Complete fares and save the money you earn.

en.searchTitle: Busdriver – Bus seating puzzle
en.summary: Seat passengers in Busdriver, a logic puzzle about reading hints, finding compatible neighbors and keeping the bus ride going.
about: Each passenger comes with a clue about where they might fit. Some neighbors raise happiness, while others cause disagreements.

Reach the hiding place
Use Space to jump and Shift to sprint. Follow the unlocked route and choose an option at the final encounter.
faq: What should I do if I reach a blocked passage?
Look for an object or a conversation you may have missed nearby. The route may depend on completing a small request first.
Do I need to talk to characters who are joking?
Yes. Their jokes sometimes contain clues about a nearby path or a quest object.
Is there more than one ending?
The final encounter offers several choices, each with a different concluding sequence.

en.summary: Keep a wobbly fighter upright, reach weapons before your rival, and use the arena's traps to make an opening in short physics-driven duels.
en.aboutTitle: Win the position before starting the fight
about: Ragdoll Arena puts two unwieldy fighters in close quarters. A small movement can turn into a tumble once you are airborne. Before chasing a dropped weapon, check what you will land on and keep enough space to stop.

Traps affect both fighters. If a rival lunges near a hazard, back away and let their momentum carry them toward it. If you rush in while your character is still rolling, it is harder to hold a weapon steady or escape the next jump.

Practice in training to learn what a short jump and a longer approach feel like. Different weapons, shields, and bonuses change how much room you need. Try new equipment where you can see its reach before relying on it close to a trap.
steps: Move in short bursts
Use A and D or the left and right arrow keys to move. Give your fighter space to regain balance.
Jump toward a clear landing
Press Space to jump and check for traps on both sides of where you expect to come down.
Aim and use equipment
Use the mouse to aim, grab a weapon, and attack when you have a clean opening.
Practise in training
Use training to learn where your fighter will land and how different weapons change your reach.
faq: Why do I tumble past where I want to stop?
The fighter keeps its momentum. Start slowing down before you reach the edge or the next hazard.
When is it worth grabbing a weapon?
Go for it when you can reach it without jumping into a trap or giving the other fighter a free attack.
Can I practise the controls before facing an opponent?
The training modes are a place to get used to jumping, aiming, and recovering your balance.

en.summary: Escape Sister Madeline's school by learning her patrol, finding puzzle items, and moving them through the halls one at a time.
en.aboutTitle: Plan an escape through the school's locked halls
about: Horror Nun puts you inside a school patrolled by Sister Madeline. You need to search rooms for clues and reach an escape route before she catches you. Listen at corners before opening up your view, and remember hiding spots as you pass them.

You carry one puzzle item at a time. If a key opens a route that also needs a tool, use the key first and leave the tool in a place you can reach again. A short, familiar route makes it easier to recover the item when the corridor is clear.

The school offers several routes out, with different requirements. Follow the clues for the route you can make progress on and check which doors your current item can open. If you hear danger approaching, crouch toward a nearby hiding spot or sprint when you have room to break away.
steps: Learn the nearby rooms
Use WASD or the arrow keys to move and the mouse to look. Note doors, lockers, and vents before going farther.
Interact with objects
Use E or left-click to examine doors and pick up puzzle items.
Listen before crossing
Crouch with C or Ctrl when you need to move quietly. Use Shift to sprint when you need to get away quickly.
Manage the item you carry
Use G to drop an item. Remember precisely where you leave it if you need to pick it up later.
faq: Can I carry a key and another tool at the same time?
You can carry one item at a time. Use the current item or leave it somewhere easy to find before taking the next one.
What can I do when Sister Madeline is close?
Listen for her approach and use the nearest available hiding spot. Lockers and vents can give you time to wait for her to pass.
Is there only one way out?
There are multiple escape routes. The puzzles and items you complete determine which route is available to you.

en.summary: Follow pursuit objectives across a 3D city and choose between a patrol car and a nimble bike as the route moves from alleys to highways.
en.aboutTitle: Choose a vehicle that suits the pursuit
about: Police Drive sets driving missions in an open 3D city. A chase can move from a wide road to a tight alley in one turn. Watch the route ahead so you can take a corner without losing so much speed that the target pulls away.

The patrol car and bike handle differently. Try the bike on routes with narrow gaps and repeated turns, or use the cruiser when a mission has longer stretches of road. Switch up your approach if you keep missing the same turn instead of trying to take it faster each time.

Completing missions opens upgraded equipment. Learn a vehicle's handling before chasing a harder objective, especially through traffic and sharp junctions. Missions involving more than one target can reward choosing a clear approach and keeping the next turn in view.
steps: Read the current objective
Check the mission and its surroundings, then pick the patrol car or the bike for the route.
Accelerate on a clear road
Press Up Arrow or W to gain speed when you have room ahead.
Set your speed before turning
Use Down Arrow or S to slow down, then steer with Left and Right or A and D.
Review which corner costs you time
If the target keeps pulling away at the same junction, slow earlier or try a vehicle that turns more easily there.
faq: Do the patrol car and motorbike handle the same way?
They respond differently to turns and narrow gaps. Try each in the city before picking one for a difficult pursuit.
How do I unlock better equipment?
Complete driving challenges and pursuit objectives in the game to make upgraded equipment available.
Why do I lose the target on tight turns?
Entering too fast can make you overshoot. Slow before the junction and accelerate again as you exit.

en.summary: Hold a rear-wheel balance through bumps and slopes, time your corrections, and unlock bikes with different handling as your runs improve.
en.aboutTitle: Keep your wheelie steady over changing terrain
about: Wheelie Master is a side-view riding game built around staying on the rear wheel. The bike's angle changes as you cross bumps or reach the top of a slope. Watch the road immediately ahead and make small corrections before a steep section forces a big one.

Use the two lean controls to keep the front wheel at a manageable height. Holding the backward lean for too long can send the bike over, while a late forward lean can end the wheelie. Save the pose controls for even ground while you learn how the bike responds.

Longer runs and wheelies help you earn gear. A different bike can change its weight and the way it responds to a familiar input, so try a short practice ride after switching. Use the first few bumps to learn how much lean brings the front wheel back down without dropping it.
steps: Raise the front wheel
Use Left Arrow to lean back and start riding on the rear wheel.
Correct an over-tilt early
Press Right Arrow to lean forward before the bike tips too far back.
Try poses on flatter sections
Use Up or Down Arrow to perform poses. Wait for a steady stretch before experimenting.
Relearn each bike's response
After an unlock, practise over the first few slopes before trying to beat your record.
faq: Why do I flip backward when I cross a bump?
A bump can add to the angle you already have. Ease forward before the front wheel rises too far.
When should I try a pose?
Try one when the wheelie is steady and the road ahead is even so you have time to correct your balance.
Do unlocked bikes ride differently?
They vary in weight and handling. Test the same lean on the new bike before trying a longer run.

en.summary: Turn taps into startup cash, buy businesses that earn while you are away, and choose when to activate short income boosts.
en.aboutTitle: Build income that keeps coming between taps
about: Early taps give you the cash for your first business. As that business earns on its own, check how much the next upgrade would add. Buying a new source of income makes more sense when upgrading the current one would take longer to pay back.

Save temporary boosters for when you have several productive businesses. Increasing ordinary revenue before applying a multiplier gives the boost more income to work on. When you plan to step away, investing in passive income can keep the next session moving.

The futuristic technology upgrades open larger multipliers as the economy grows. Weekly country competitions add a shared leaderboard. You can work on your own income first and contribute to a team once you have a steady flow of earnings.
steps: Start the cash flow
Click or tap to earn enough money for your first business.
Buy an income source
Use the earnings to buy a business, then compare its next upgrade with another available purchase.
Time your boost
Activate a booster when your most productive businesses are running.
Spend income when you return
Check the money earned while away and look for upgrades that raise future passive income.
faq: Does the game earn money while I am away?
Owned businesses generate offline income, so passive upgrades keep working between sessions.
When is a boost most effective?
Use it after improving regular earnings or buying a major business, so the multiplication applies to more income.
What is the weekly competition?
Country teams combine their progress to compete for leaderboard positions and rewards.

en.summary: Choose a fighter class, practise the timing of both special skills, and tune your equipment for fantasy duels or Survival Tower waves.
en.aboutTitle: Build a fighter for the next arena
about: Tiny Arena gives you four classes with different skill and equipment options. Try the basic attack and both specials early. A class that makes space comfortably can be easier to learn than one that expects you to stay within reach of a large enemy.

Opponents grow tougher as the arenas advance. Watch a new enemy act before spending both specials. If your first skill creates a chance to move, use that space to decide whether the second skill can land safely.

Weapons, armor, and artifacts change how a class performs. Adjust your loadout based on where you are losing. Survival Tower keeps the pressure on across multiple waves and puts currency at risk, so practise with unfamiliar equipment in a regular duel first.
steps: Choose a class
Read the available skills and pick a fighter whose basic attack is comfortable to use.
Get into range
Move with A and D or the left and right arrow keys. Press Space for the basic attack.
Use specials one at a time
Press J or K for the respective special and keep one available while sizing up a new opponent.
Review equipment after the fight
Compare damage and protection before changing your weapon, armor, or artifact.
faq: Why do classes feel different?
A class determines which skills and types of gear you can use, which changes the openings you can take.
What is Survival Tower?
It is a wave challenge where you risk earned currency for rewards as the fights get tougher.
What should I change if a big enemy keeps winning?
Try more protection if you run out of health early. If you survive but cannot finish the duel, review your attack and skill timing.

en.summary: Fight through city districts with punches, kicks, grabs, and blocks. Learn where to stand before a crowd closes in.
en.aboutTitle: Make space between fights in the city
about: City Brawl takes you through city blocks where enemies can approach from either side. Move toward a clear patch of the screen when a group builds up. Having one side free makes it easier to see when a fighter is about to move in.

Punches, kicks, grabs, and blocks give you several ways to handle an encounter. Keep the first exchange short while you learn an enemy’s reach. Boss fights add patterns of their own, so watch for the pause after a move before trying a longer combo.

Street victories, quests, and achievements contribute to progression. Fighters vary in speed and power. Choose upgrades around what is holding you back. Faster movement can help when you are repeatedly cornered, while power helps if you already get regular openings.
steps: Move around the group
Use WASD or the arrow keys to move and Space to jump.
Test your reach
Use Z to punch or X to kick. Start with one input so you can see how far it reaches.
Grab or block
Use C to grab and V to block. Give yourself time to move after an exchange.
Watch a boss repeat a move
Identify when the attack ends and take that opening before trying a longer combo.
faq: Why do I keep getting hit from behind?
Opponents can approach from several directions. Move out of the middle of a group before starting another combo.
How do I block or grab?
Press V to block and C to grab.
Do all fighters move at the same pace?
Fighters vary in power and speed. Try a few encounters before committing upgrades to a new character.

en.summary: Chase a coin-stealing raccoon through snowy routes. Change lanes, jump, or slide as penguins and snowmen block the path.
en.aboutTitle: Find the clear lane before taking the coins
about: Santa Run sends Santa after a raccoon through a winter obstacle course. Look for the next safe lane while you collect gold. A coin trail can be tempting, but following it too far can leave you facing a snowman with little time to move.

Some obstacles need a jump or slide while others are easier to go around. Watch the obstacle after the one in front of you. Switching lanes early gives you time to prepare a jump or slide without making both decisions at once.

The scenery and hazard combinations change as you progress. Treat a new section as a chance to learn the timing, especially when icy patches are close together. A longer run gives you more opportunities to collect coins than a risky detour for one short line.
steps: Steer into a clear lane
Press Left or Right Arrow, or use A and D, to move sideways.
Jump over low obstacles
Press Up Arrow or W when you are close enough to clear the obstacle.
Slide under barriers
Press Down Arrow or S to slide when the route has room underneath.
Choose safe coin trails
Look beyond the last coin before committing to a lane.
faq: Should I follow every row of coins?
Take a coin row when you can also see a way around the next obstacle.
How do I slide?
Press Down Arrow or S to slide beneath a barrier.
Does the route stay the same?
The winter environments and combinations of obstacles change during the run. Watch the next section as it comes into view.

en.summary: Hold and release Up Arrow to balance a bike on its rear wheel. Keep the angle steady as you ride along a 2D highway.
en.aboutTitle: Control the wheelie with short corrections
about: Wheelie Party gives you a single key for lifting the front wheel. Holding Up Arrow raises the bike, and releasing it changes the angle back toward the road. The run is about feeling how much tilt builds before the bike becomes hard to recover.

Start with a gentle lift and release when the bike is already high enough. If the front wheel begins to drop, a short press can bring it back up. Several small corrections are easier to judge than one long hold after the bike has started leaning too far.

Watch the front wheel relative to the horizon as you gain distance. The bright highway gives you a clear reference for the bike’s angle. If one run ends in a backward tip, release a little earlier at the same angle in the next attempt.
steps: Raise the front wheel
Hold Up Arrow until you have a visible, moderate wheelie.
Release before the angle gets steep
Let go of Up Arrow as the front wheel climbs too high.
Catch a falling front wheel
Use a brief press to bring it back up when it starts dropping.
Repeat the same opening
Practise a consistent first lift, then adjust the length of later taps to keep going.
faq: Why do I flip backward?
A hold that lasts too long keeps increasing the bike’s angle. Release earlier on the next lift.
Do I need a separate brake key?
This version uses a held Up Arrow and its release to control the front wheel.
How can I make a wheelie last longer?
Keep the front wheel at a moderate height and use short corrections before the bike develops a large tilt.

en.summary: Jump a colorful ball along music-synced stairs and platforms. Learn each track’s gaps to keep the sequence going and unlock more songs.
en.aboutTitle: Read the stairs and listen for your next jump
about: Bounce Path follows Blob through courses built around songs. A click makes the ball jump. The challenge is judging where the ball will be when you tap, especially when the next platform is higher or farther than the last one.

Listen for a steady beat on the opening stretch and watch how the landings line up with it. If you miss a jump, note the obstacle it happened at. Try the same opening again and change the timing of that jump first.

Later tracks make the timing less forgiving by changing platform patterns or the pace. Improve the opening route until it needs less attention. That leaves you more time to look ahead when a new gap or obstacle appears.
steps: Start a track
Watch the first few stairs and listen for the song’s rhythm.
Jump with one input
Left-click to make Blob jump as it reaches the next gap or step.
Look past the landing
Check the next obstacle before you make the current jump.
Practise a difficult sequence
Repeat the track and change the timing at the first missed jump before trying to improve the whole run.
faq: How do I control the ball?
Use the left mouse button to jump. Timing that input carries the ball through the track.
Why do I miss even when I tap to the music?
Look at the gap as well as listening. The platform layout tells you which beat gives the ball room to land.
Can I unlock more songs?
Progress through the available tracks to open additional songs with their own layouts.

en.summary: Build barricades, manage weapons and supplies between zombie waves, and try unlocked equipment freely in Playground.
en.aboutTitle: Spend your supplies where the defense is weakest
about: Undead Invasion combines shooting with building defenses across a side-scrolling battlefield. Each wave puts pressure on the headquarters. Check where enemies are coming from before buying a new barricade or trap, especially if one side has already taken most of the damage.

Plan for reloads and repairs. Use quiet periods to restore the part of your defense that failed first. If your structures are holding but you are running short of firepower, a weapon upgrade may do more for the next wave than an extra wall.

Available upgrades can vary between runs. Let what you find shape the plan for that attempt. Playground lets you use unlocked items without the same risk of ending a run, so it is useful for testing how two pieces of equipment work together.
steps: Choose Defense or Playground
Pick Defense for escalating waves or Playground to try equipment without the wave pressure.
Move, attack, and reload
Use the arrow keys to move, click to attack, and press R to reload.
Switch your equipment
Press Q to change weapons and use the fence icon to build a structure.
Check the front before the next wave
Spend resources where the previous wave came closest to breaking through.
faq: Can I try a trap before buying it in a run?
Playground lets you experiment with equipment you have already unlocked.
How do I reload or switch weapons?
Press R to reload and Q to switch weapons.
Should I spend on walls or weapons first?
Repair an opening if enemies are getting through. If your barriers hold and you still cannot clear a wave, put more of the next budget toward firepower.

en.summary: Take a stickman fighter through monster-filled arenas, unlock class skills, and manage attack cooldowns when enemies close in.
en.aboutTitle: Keep one move available when the next wave closes in
about: Stickman War uses side-scrolling arenas where enemies can fill the space in front of your fighter. Move enough to keep an opening behind you. That gives you somewhere to dash when too many monsters crowd the same stretch.

Basic attacks and special abilities serve different parts of a fight. Use normal strikes while the approach is clear, then spend a skill when there are enough enemies in reach to make it count. Using everything together can leave you waiting through several cooldowns.

Class progression opens more skills and gear. Learn the range and recovery of an ability before bringing it into a boss fight. If a new group keeps catching you between attacks, try an upgrade that helps with recovery or use the dash earlier.
steps: Move into a clear part of the arena
Press A or D to move and W to jump past incoming threats.
Use the basic strike
Press J to attack when an enemy is in reach.
Dash to reset your position
Press K when you need room or want to leave a crowded section.
Space out special abilities
Use Numpad 1 through 4 for available specials. Keep an ability ready for a second group.
faq: How do I unlock more skills?
Earn experience and currency in fights, then spend upgrades in the available paths for your class.
Which key makes my fighter dash?
Press K to dash.
Why save an ability?
Specials need time to recover. Saving one gives you an option if a new group arrives while the others are unavailable.

en.summary: Climb uneven rock trails with careful throttle and steering. Tune your crawler and improve routes over narrow ridges and steep climbs.
en.aboutTitle: Build enough momentum for the climb without tipping
about: Mad Trails asks you to drive over steep slopes, loose rocks, and narrow ridges. The tires react to the terrain and can lose grip if you accelerate hard while the crawler is already tilted. Look for a line that stays steady before carrying more speed up the hill.

Too little throttle can strand you partway up a climb. Start the approach with enough speed to keep moving, then ease off before the crest. If the front of the crawler starts lifting too far, a gentler approach can help more than another push against the same rock.

Successful runs unlock vehicles and tuning options for grip, torque, and suspension. Try one change on a route you already know. A ghost run gives you a reference for finding slow corners and climbs once you can finish the course reliably.
steps: Approach the climb
Use Up Arrow or W to go forward and line up a steady route over the obstacle.
Reverse to try another line
Press Down Arrow or S if the crawler wedges against a rock or loses its approach.
Use small steering corrections
Steer with the left and right arrow keys or A and D while crossing a narrow ridge.
Compare a tuning change
Try the same climb before and after an upgrade so you can tell how it affects your grip.
faq: Why does the crawler tip on steep climbs?
Too much throttle at a steep angle can lift the front and flip the vehicle. Approach more gently and ease off near the crest.
What affects how crawlers handle?
Different vehicles vary in torque, grip, and suspension. The best choice depends on the terrain.
When is a ghost useful?
Once you can finish the course, it helps show where a better line or a slower approach could save time.

en.summary: Time a single click to drive the baseball for distance. Spend the coins from each hit on strength, swing speed, or bounce.
en.aboutTitle: Find a repeatable swing before spending on distance
about: Bat Smash measures how far the ball travels after you hit it. Watch the ball reach the hitting area and click at the point that gets the best contact. A consistent swing is a better way to measure progress than changing the timing on every attempt.

Distance earns coins that you can put into strength, swing speed, or bounce. They improve different parts of a hit. If the ball travels well in the air but stops quickly on the ground, bounce is a reasonable next upgrade to try.

The game gives you distance milestones and new bats to unlock. When you change a stat or equip a new bat, compare several well-timed hits. One unlucky swing can hide whether the new setup is giving you a better result.
steps: Watch the incoming ball
Follow it into the hitting area before pressing anything.
Click to swing
Click once when the ball reaches your best contact point.
Choose a distance upgrade
Use coins earned on the hit to improve strength, speed, or bounce.
Compare several attempts
Try the upgraded setup on a few well-timed swings before spending again.
faq: How do I swing?
Click once as the ball reaches the hitting area. Timing decides the quality of contact.
What does the bounce upgrade do?
It improves the ball’s travel after it hits the ground, so it can add distance beyond the first landing.
How do I get different bats?
Progress through the game and reach its reward milestones to unlock more bat designs.
